candidate.title: Directed residual tangent transport with pair-separation guard
candidate.equation: For valid rows define residual r = y - x, midpoint z = (x + y) / 2, and unit residual direction v = r / (||r||_2 + epsilon). For each endpoint, use its stop-gradient nearest codeword c_s or c_t. Let a_i = (c_i - z) - ((c_i - z) dot v) v be the codeword offset projected onto the subspace orthogonal to the residual. Define L = w * mean[||a_t - (a_s + gamma v)||_2^2 + eta * relu(delta - ||c_t - c_s||_2)^2].

symbols.x: source representation, source row of source
symbols.y: target representation, corresponding row of target
symbols.v: unit direction of the source-to-target residual
symbols.c_s: codebook vector nearest to x under the current hard assignment
symbols.c_t: codebook vector nearest to y under the current hard assignment
symbols.a_s: source codeword offset from z projected orthogonally to v
symbols.a_t: target codeword offset from z projected orthogonally to v
symbols.gamma: desired directed displacement along the residual direction
symbols.delta: minimum desired separation between the pair's assigned codewords
symbols.mask: valid-row indicator; only valid rows contribute to the masked mean

candidate.behaviour_signal: The ordered residual y - x, which sets the transport direction and distinguishes source from target.
candidate.codebook_interaction: The transport term moves the endpoint codewords toward a residual-conditioned relative geometry in the subspace orthogonal to the pair's behaviour direction; it does not ask both codewords to meet at the midpoint or at a shared target. The additional hinge pushes the assigned pair codewords apart when their distance is below delta and has zero gradient otherwise. Assignments are stop-gradient. The transport's residual and midpoint dependence may still move codewords indirectly, so pair-distance and global occupancy must be measured.
candidate.encoder_interaction: The residual-conditioned term has nonzero gradients to source and target representations before host assembly. Those auxiliary encoder gradients are discarded by the host; the nonzero codebook gradients provide the effective route to changing exported SIDs.
candidate.risk: Residual directions can be noisy or nearly zero, and a local tangent-space geometry objective may reorganize codewords without preserving the useful global prefix tree. The separation hinge prevents direct pair convergence below its threshold but cannot stop unrelated codewords from becoming crowded or assignments from becoming imbalanced. The resulting geometry could raise the pair metric yet worsen retrieval or train-to-test stability.
candidate.falsifier: Reject if swapping source and target leaves the loss unchanged, any declared gradient is zero or non-finite on valid probe inputs, or the frozen evaluation fails to raise pair ER while meeting all structure constraints and improving Stage-3 recall@10 over 0.06406796775709883.
candidate.why_not_the_measured_failures: Unlike residual transport that reaches only the encoder, this objective differentiates through selected codebook vectors, so its effect survives the host's gradient overwrite. Unlike the collapsed pairwise curvature and shared-code assignment mechanisms, it transports endpoint codewords in a behaviour-conditioned tangent geometry and includes an explicit lower bound on pair separation instead of rewarding endpoint convergence. Its residual-conditioned geometry is mathematically distinct from the assignment-information and direct margin-geometry candidates.
